I also read the definitions of matrixData, entry and entry_matrixData in QuantumFixedPauliProgram.lean, and grepped the repo for uses of entry (matrixData ...) and for the two round-trip theorems. The file has no simp attributes and uses only `simp only`, so the one issue is about the missing simp interface for the matrixData/entry round trip. I did not run Lean. I am unsure whether `simp only [entry_matrixData]` closes the goals directly after the attribute is added. It should, because simp rewrites under the binders and `fun s t => A s t` eta-reduces. I did not judge the opaque program definitions, since they are outside this rubric.

findings.declaration: gramData_matrixData and rebitData_matrixData (missing @[simp] on entry_matrixData, eta-form workaround repeated)
findings.excerpt:
have h : (fun s t : β => entry (matrixData A) s t) = A := by
    funext s t

  simp only [gramData,h]
findings.problem: The round-trip lemma `entry_matrixData : entry (matrixData A) s t = A s t` is not tagged `@[simp]`. It is the canonical normal form, since it eliminates the encoding `entry (matrixData A)`. Every caller therefore rebuilds the same eta-expanded equation `(fun s t => entry (matrixData A) s t) = A` by hand with `funext` and `exact`, and passes it to `simp only`. The identical four-line block appears in both theorems here (lines 46-49 and 79-82). It appears again in QuantumFixedPauliProgram.lean (`he`, around line 110) and QuantumPaddedSampling.lean (`hE`, line 26). The file's simp interface for these round trips is therefore ad hoc.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `entry_matrixData` in QuantumFixedPauliProgram.lean as `@[simp]`. The left side has `matrixData` as head argument and the right side is strictly smaller, so there is no loop and no competing rule. Then rewrite the proofs here as `simp only [gramData, entry_matrixData]` and `simp only [rebitData, entry_matrixData]`. These should work because simp rewrites under the `fun s t` binders and eta-reduces `fun s t => A s t` to `A`. Alternatively, state a companion simp lemma `(fun s t => entry (matrixData A) s t) = A` once. The `have h` blocks in the four places can then be deleted.
findings.benefit: Four copies of the same boilerplate go away. Later `gramData`/`rebitData`-style lemmas get the round trip automatically from `simp`, with no hand-built eta equation. The normal form for `entry (matrixData A)` becomes explicit and discoverable.
